title: PRD: Stochastic Sensitivity and Rollback Decision Tree for Optimize Evals
creator: Leah Chen
body:
Summary: This PRD defines a robust, statistically-grounded evaluation and rollback framework for Redwood Optimize. The goal is to reduce noise-driven rollouts, surface real regressions earlier, and codify automated decision boundaries for canary/A-B rollouts. The doc covers: promptset curation & weighting, sensitivity analysis and statistical tests, multi-metric acceptance windows, staged rollout criteria, automatic rollback triggers, and observability/alerting playbooks.

Background & motivation: Teams using Optimize run model swaps, quantization or batching changes, and routing policies that can alter output quality subtly. Current practice relies on a mix of manual checks and ad-hoc thresholds which lead to two failure modes: (1) missed regressions because signal is noisy and sample sizes small; (2) false-positive rollbacks when transient sampling noise or distribution shift triggers a gate. Optimize needs an evaluation framework that is: 1) statistically principled (controls false positives/negatives), 2) practical for typical PLG usage patterns (fast canaries, limited promptset sizes), and 3) operational (clear alerts, human-in-loop escalation).

Goals (measurable):
- Reduce false-positive rollback rate by >50% for canary rollouts vs current baseline (measured over historical rollouts).
- Detect true customer-visible regressions (customer-impact medium/high) within 24 hours of rollout with >90% sensitivity for regressions >=5% absolute drop on primary metrics.
- Provide a documented decision tree that enables automated stop/rollback for high-severity regressions and advisory alerts for low-severity ones.

Non-goals:
- Replacing model-level unit tests or offline evaluations (this is a production canary/evaluation layer).
- Building a fully general statistical library for all experiment types — scope is Optimize repo canonical canary and A/B flows.

Promptset curation and sampling strategy:
- Promptset composition: canonical Evaluate-Set (EvalSet) will be curated with balanced buckets: Intent types (25%), Difficulty (25%), Context length distribution (short/medium/long = 40%), Safety-sensitive examples (10%). Each EvalSet should be sized to support reliable detection at the target sensitivity (see sample size guidance below).
- Weighting: During analysis, examples are weighted to mirror production traffic (intent & length weights derived from last 30 days). Weights are stored with the EvalSet to permit reproducible analysis.
- Versioning & provenance: Every EvalSet gets a stable id (optimize-evalset-vN), a curator, and a one-line rationale. EvalSets are immutable once used for a rollout; new edits create new versions.
- Sampling matrix: For fast canaries, support two sample strata: quick-check (n~200 weighted examples) and full-check (n~2000). Quick-check is used pre-rollout and for immediate alarms; full-check runs as a background job across the first 24 hours of rollout.

Statistical tests, sensitivity, and thresholds:
- Primary metrics: choose 1 primary metric per rollout (e.g., authoritative QA Exact Match, Answerness-Precision, task-specific utility score). Secondary metrics: safety score, hallucination rate, latency (p99), token cost.
- Hypothesis framing: we use non-inferiority tests for most rollouts. Null: new variant is worse than baseline by margin delta. Alternative: new variant is within delta (non-inferior) or better. Default non-inferiority margin: 3% absolute for primary metrics unless product owner specifies otherwise.
- Tests & multiple comparisons: Adopt bootstrap CIs (95%) for primary effect size; for multiple secondary metrics apply Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction to control for false discoveries across k metrics.
- Sensitivity/sample size guidance: To detect a 5% absolute shift with 90% power at alpha=0.05, recommend full-check n>=1500 (weighted). Quick-check (n~200) is expected to catch only large regressions (>10-12%); its role is fast triage not final acceptance.
- Drift detection: Continuously compute embedding distribution drift (cosine similarity) vs baseline. Trigger deeper analysis if average cosine similarity drops below 0.92 or KL divergence over categorical buckets increases by >0.12.

A/B and canary criteria (staged rollout rules):
- Canary phase (0->5% traffic): run quick-check online and full-check background. Conditions to proceed to ramp: primary metric non-inferiority confirmed (95% CI for difference lies above -delta) AND no critical safety regression (see rollback rules). If quick-check shows a large negative effect (>10% drop) immediately halt rollout.
- Ramp phase (5->25%): full-check must maintain non-inferiority over sliding 24-hour windows. If a secondary metric degrades but within agreed tolerances (see acceptance section) mark advisory and continue; if exceeds tolerances, trigger stop.
- A/B experiments: use two-sided permutation tests for randomized A/B. Require pre-registered primary metric and sample size; apply sequential analysis boundaries (alpha-spending) to avoid false positives from peeking.

Automated rollback decision tree (summary):
- Severity tiers:
  - Tier 1 (Critical): any customer-facing regression classified as high (e.g., major correctness drop on paid customer queries, SLO violation >5% absolute) OR safety violation above threshold (toxicity > baseline + 0.5 std). Action: immediate automated rollback and page on-call.
  - Tier 2 (Major): primary metric drop between 3% and 5% absolute over 24h with p<0.05. Action: pause ramp, create incident-notice, require manual approve to continue.
  - Tier 3 (Minor): secondary metric degrade or primary drop <3%. Action: advisory alert to product owner and runbook review; no automatic rollback.
- Fail-safe: any latency p99 increase >25% or token cost increase >15% triggers automatic rollback.

Acceptance criteria (what must be true before this ticket is Done):
- Implementation: automated evaluation job that runs quick-check on canary launch and full-check continuously for 24h; job writes results to Optimize dashboard and emits structured alerts.
- Decision engine: server-side decision tree encoding the tiers above and webhook to trigger rollback action in the routing plane.
- Dashboards: new Optimize Eval dashboard tiles showing primary/secondary metrics, bootstrap CIs, embedding drift, and a canary timeline view.
- Runbooks & docs: published runbook describing action steps for each tier, escalation contacts, and postmortem template.
- Tests: integration tests that simulate three synthetic failure modes (large regression, small persistent regression, drift) and assert the correct automation response.
- Stakeholder sign-off: PM (Leah Chen), Reliability lead (Ravi Singh), Safety lead (Marta Ortega) and Solutions Eng sign-off on rollout thresholds.

Monitoring, alerting & observability:
- Alerts: three alert channels: advisory Slack digest, P1 PagerDuty, and email incident-notice for stakeholders. Alert payload includes effect size, CI, sample sizes, and top failing buckets.
- Telemetry: store per-example outcomes, model version ids, EvalSet id, timestamp and routing shard for reproducibility and debugging. Retain sampled traces for 90 days.
- Post-rollout regression check: scheduled job at 24h, 72h, and 7d that recomputes metrics on recent traffic and flags delayed regressions.

Dependencies and integrations:
- Routing plane: ability to pause/reroute traffic programmatically (engineering dependency ENG-2139).
- Dashboard and alerting infra: hooks to emit structured events (ENG-2494).
- EvalSet storage/versioning: canonical storage location and API (ENG-2712).

Open questions & trade-offs:
- Default non-inferiority margin: is 3% too strict for some tasks? We plan to allow per-rollout overrides with documented justification.
- Quick-check false negatives: we accept some risk of missed small regressions in quick-check to preserve speed. Full-check mitigates this.
- Complexity vs visibility: how much of the decision tree is automated vs surfaced to humans? Default is automated for Tier 1 and safety rollbacks; Tier 2 requires manual approval to continue.

Next steps & milestones:
- Week 1: finalize thresholds and EvalSet template; ship quick-check job (canary launch hook).
- Week 2-3: implement full-check job, dashboard tiles, and alerting.
- Week 4: run synthetic experiments and stakeholder review; adjust thresholds.
- Week 5: enable automated Tier 1 rollbacks behind feature flag and run shadow mode for 2 weeks, then flip on.

acceptance_criteria: 1) Quick-check runs at canary start and emits result payload to Optimize dashboard. 2) Full-check background job computes bootstrap CIs and FDR-corrected secondary metrics and writes artifacts to storage. 3) Decision engine implements Tier 1 auto-rollback and Tier 2 pause-with-notice. 4) Dashboards and runbooks published and accessible to SRE/PMs. 5) Integration tests covering the three synthetic failure modes pass in CI.
requirements: - EvalSet format and versioning API. - Quick-check online scorer integrated into canary path. - Full-check batch job with bootstrap CI implementation. - Decision engine webhook to routing plane. - Dashboard tiles and PagerDuty escalation mapping.
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy quick-check in read-only mode to collect baseline signals for 72h. 2) Enable quick-check gating at 0% traffic (simulate). 3) Turn on quick-check gating for real canaries behind feature flag. 4) Deploy full-check and dashboards; run in shadow for 14 days. 5) Activate Tier 1 auto-rollback behind feature flag; shadow for 2 weeks. 6) Flip on for all canaries after stakeholder sign-off.
monitoring_and_alerting: - Advisory Slack digest (daily) for minor drifts. - PagerDuty for Tier 1 auto-rollback and critical safety violations. - Email incident-notice to product & reliability on Tier 2 events. - Dashboard shows effect sizes, CIs, sample sizes, embedding drift, and top buckets contributing to regressions.
notes: Designed to balance speed of PLG rollouts with statistical rigor. Will revisit non-inferiority margins after two months of real rollout data.
decision_history: 2026-03-10 Leah Chen created PRD. 2026-03-12 Thresholds reviewed with SRE and Safety; agreed on 3% default non-inferiority margin and Tier definitions. 2026-03-13 Engineering capacity confirmed; target feature-flag timeline set.
